changes.author: giskard09
changes.title: RFC: Signed receipts for Haystack pipeline component calls
changes.text: Point 3 is one we've been building toward in this exact thread — back in June, replying to @arian-gogani's point here: "each receipt carries the hash of the previous one in the run, so retriever chunk → ranker → generator output verifies as an ordered whole, not as disconnected signatures." What's shipped since then is `trail-head-ref-v1` (argentum-core): head/prev_head chaining with named failure modes for exactly the removal case — `seq_gap` (a removed record leaves a gap), `head_mismatch` (a record's own hash doesn't recompute), `link_mismatch` (the next record's prev_head doesn't match). changes.author: giskard09
changes.title: feature request: optional `action_ref` field in send_token's result
changes.text: Understood, thanks for discussing it with the team. One clarification for anyone finding this later: `action_ref` isn't about uniqueness — txHash already covers that. It's a content-addressed hash of the *declared* request fields (network/to/amount/token/timestamp), computable by anyone from those same fields — so if the result is later re-stated by someone other than the CLI, a verifier can confirm the restated fields are exactly the ones originally declared, without trusting whoever is now reporting them. changes.text: This is the two-layer split `trail-head-ref-v1` (argentum-core) ships: `continuity` is the hash chain — removes/reorders break the link, same test you named here, Daniel. `completeness` is a periodic checkpoint anchored outside the log owner's control, catching exactly what Klenio's Case 3 just confirmed by construction: tail truncation, which continuity alone can't see (a shorter log and a truncated one look identical internally). changes.text: This closes exactly the gap we said we didn't have an answer to — and the `corpus_digest` move (claim becomes derivation, not assertion) is the same principle our own specs run on, just applied one layer down from where we work. Good, honest write-up of the costs too (latency, the encoder-quality caveat) — appreciate it.

changes.text: This is the exact property `trail-head-ref-v1` (argentum-core, draft/reference-implementation status — not yet live in our own pipeline) is built for, same shape as `decision_window`, with one difference worth naming: ours checkpoints `seq`+`head` once per period and anchors the period's Merkle root on-chain (`AnchorRegistry.anchor(bytes32)`), rather than self-signing a window. The reason: a `window_signature` signed by the same PEP that emits the log doesn't establish independence — if it can sign a window, it can sign a shorter one after truncating.
